evidence: Plin. NH 12.22: (rāmī) īmī in terram adeō curvantur, ut … (Lewis & Short s.v. curvō)
Plin. NH 1 (contents of book 12): fīcus Indica
terms.comment: Pliny’s Indian fig, whose lowest branches bend down into the earth and take root, so that one tree makes a grove round itself: the banyan. The botanists call it Fīcus benghalēnsis; the sacred fig of Indian temples is Fīcus religiōsa.

phrases.latin: Sub fīcū Indicā cōnsīdāmus: umbram dēnsam praebet.
phrases.english: Let’s sit down under the banyan: it gives deep shade.

phrases.latin: Vidē rādīcēs quae dē rāmīs pendent!
phrases.english: Look at the roots hanging from the branches!
